name: browser-tools
about: Re-tests the browser tools' fixes of 8 Nov 2026 (the lab's browser report) in three questions, on Wikipedia, MDN and example.com: scroll's position after the scroll, scroll_to by ref, tab on the page tools, 'changed' after hover / PageDown / a click that opens a box, Escape closing a hover popup, Enter after typing, a dropdown choice, find_pictures' lead image, the bad-ref error; then the gaps closed the same day, in two more: a double click (the word selected), a right-click, a tab at a desktop width (MDN's search a box, its shot saying the width), a frame from another site said as one, a same-origin frame read and a drag in it (jQuery UI's sortable demo). Turns 4 and 5 carry the fake AI's calls, so they run on a --fake --live-web lab too. Each turn's shots (thread, panel, page; light and dark) show what the checks can't: the lead image, the preview, where each page ended up.

steps.note: 1. Scrolling, scroll_to by ref, the lead picture (Wikipedia's Lighthouse: long, with an infobox picture).

steps.ask: This is a test of your browser tools: use them exactly as asked, one step at a time, and keep your answer short. 1. Open https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse beside the chat with browser_navigate. 2. Scroll it down two screens with browser_scroll (direction down, amount 2) and tell me the y position its result reports. 3. Read the page with browser_read in mode "elements", take the ref of the link to the article's History section (or its heading), and scroll to it with browser_scroll_to using that ref (not text); tell me the y position it reports. 4. Use find_pictures on this page and show me the article's lead image (the first picture, at the top of the article) with show_picture.

steps.note: Scroll reports where it ended (not where it started); scroll_to scrolls by ref; find_pictures offers a picture to show.
Is the picture shown the article's lead image? The thread's shot says.
2. Hover, Escape, PageDown, a second tab, tab on find and scroll, a ref that isn't there.

steps.ask: Still testing, one step at a time, short answers. 1. On the Lighthouse page (tab 1), use browser_read in mode "elements", then browser_hover over the first link in the article's first paragraph (Wikipedia shows a preview of the linked article when you point at a link); tell me what the hover's result says changed. 2. Press Escape with browser_key; tell me what changed. 3. Press PageDown with browser_key; tell me what changed. 4. Open https://example.com/ in a new tab with browser_tabs (action new). 5. Without switching back, use browser_find with tab 1 to find the word "lantern" on the Lighthouse page, and browser_scroll with tab 1 to scroll that page down one screen. 6. On tab 2, click ref 9999 with browser_click (there's no such element) and copy its error word for word.

steps.note: 'changed' after a hover and PageDown says what changed; find and scroll take tab; a ref that was never there isn't blamed on the page changing.
Escape closes the hover preview (soft: it depends on Wikipedia's previews showing for a pointer that isn't a mouse).
3. A dropdown, a click that opens a box, typing then Enter (Wikipedia's Special:AllPages, MDN's search).

steps.ask: Last part, one step at a time, short answers. 1. Open https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:AllPages beside the chat. With browser_form_input, set its Namespace dropdown to "Help", and tell me what the result says it did. 2. Open https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/table. Click its search button or box at the top with browser_click, and tell me what the click's result says changed. 3. Type flexbox into that search box with browser_type (no submit), then press Enter with browser_key, and tell me where you ended up.

steps.note: A dropdown's choice isn't called typing; Enter after typing submits the search through the submit check (a search asks nothing).
The click that opens MDN's search box says something changed (soft: MDN's header at the panel's width decides whether there's a box to open).
4. A double click, a right-click and a desktop width (Wikipedia's Lighthouse; MDN's table page, whose live example is a frame from another site).

fake.content: Double-clicked and right-clicked the title; read MDN at the panel's width and at a desktop width.

steps.ask: Testing new browser tools, one step at a time, short answers. 1. Open https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse beside the chat. 2. Find the article's first paragraph ("A lighthouse is a tower…") with browser_find, double-click it with browser_click (count 2) and tell me what its result says was selected. 3. Right-click that paragraph (button right) and tell me what changed. 4. Open https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/table in a new tab with browser_tabs (action new). 5. Read it in mode "elements" and take a browser_screenshot: is its search a box or a button? 6. Lay that tab out at a desktop width with browser_tabs (action width, width 1280), read it again in mode "elements" and take another browser_screenshot: is the search a box now? 7. Read it with browser_read: does it say it has a frame Yap can't read inside (its live example)?

steps.note: A double click selects the word there; a right-click says what it did (no menu of the page's own: said so); a tab laid out at a desktop width, its shot saying so.

At 1280 px MDN draws its desktop layout (a search box in its header: the page shot shows it; the read lists it as MDN's own button, 'Search the site') and its live example, a frame from another site (mdnplay.dev), listed as one Yap can't reach inside (soft: MDN decides).
A plain read says the page has a frame Yap can't read inside (soft: MDN's page decides).
5. A same-origin frame read and a drag in it (jQuery UI's sortable demo: a list in a frame of the site's own).

fake.content: Item 3 is higher in the list now.

steps.ask: Last one, step by step, short answers. 1. Open https://jqueryui.com/sortable/ beside the chat and read it with browser_read: its demo list is in a frame; which items does the read show? 2. Find "Item 3" and "Item 1" with browser_find, then drag Item 3 onto Item 1 with browser_drag (from and to by ref). 3. Tell me what the drag's result says changed, and take a browser_screenshot.

steps.note: A same-origin frame's words are read with the page; a drag inside it goes through.
The drag's 'changed' says where Item 3 went (soft: jQuery UI decides where an item lands).
